The derived profile-*-flat.txt / profile-*-callgraph.txt reports and the perf-stat-*.txt counters are promoted and hashed, and every profile number in the report is read from those. The .data files themselves are dispensable work and were DELETED at query completion together with the rest of work/Q22 (SSOT section 19: 'promote required files to raw and delete dispensable work'). They are reproducible from raw/Q22/hltel_profile_driver.sh against the pinned binaries.

notes: Q22 WAS FULLY RE-MEASURED after a section 9 cpuset violation was found, and the pre-remediation artifacts are retained under invalid-affinity-20260802/ with INVALID.json and valid=false. Root cause: CUBRID caches its affinity mask ONCE at process start (src/base/resources.cpp:204-218 affinity_cpuset() inside the function-local static of resources::effective(), whose own comment says it 'must be called first in the main thread's entry point') and rebinds every pooled thread it creates later to that cached mask (src/base/resources.cpp:174-188 clearaffinity() -> pthread_setaffinity_np). cub_server pid 2646189 had been started with a mask of CPUs 24-31, so although the running server's existing TIDs had been taskset to 0-15, every thread created afterwards -- INCLUDING ALL FIVE parallel-query workers of every statement -- executed on CPUs 24-31, outside the contracted SUT set. The affinity guard measured those workers at 16.5-16.8 core-seconds EACH, off-cpuset.

WHY THE PRE/POST TID GATE DID NOT CATCH IT, and what was added. The stage 14.1 preflight at 20:44:39 reported 'TOTAL engine tids=30 off_cpuset=0 -> PASS' and was correct at that instant: parallel-query workers exist only while a statement runs, so an idle-server check cannot see them. The postflight caught only the two leftover 'transaction' threads. harness/affinity_guard.py is therefore a NEW campaign harness that samples EVERY engine TID for the whole of a stage at 0.1 s and returns CLEAN only if no engine TID was ever observed outside CPUs 0-15; every re-measured stage carries a Q22-<stage>-affinity.json verdict beside it. This is the SSOT section 24 entry 'new pooled threads escaped cpuset -> all-TID pre/post validation and invalidation', strengthened from a pre/post pair to continuous sampling.

REMEDIATION. 'reapply affinity and rerun' alone does not converge on this defect: the offending threads are created DURING the run, so three consecutive guarded attempts at CUBRID block 3 were rejected with 5 fresh off-cpuset parallel-query workers each (Q22-cubrid-block3-affinity-a{1,2,3}.json). cub_server was therefore stopped and restarted THROUGH THE MANDATORY WRAPPER (.claude/skills/cubrid-server-control/scripts/cubrid-server-ctl.sh) under 'taskset -c 0-15', so that resources::effective() caches the campaign cpuset itself. All 38 re-measured stages were then accepted on their FIRST guarded attempt.

THE PER-TID SAMPLER UNDERCOUNTS POSTGRESQL, and the card discloses it instead of hiding it. One section 12 block was observed by both instruments simultaneously: perf stat attached to the postmaster before the block's connection existed measured 6.85546 core-s of task-clock where the sampler measured 5.38 core-s over the same block, a 27.4% undercount. The cause is that PostgreSQL's parallel workers are separate processes living ~0.157 s (the InitPlan's four) and ~0.44 s (the main pipeline's one), so a 25 ms /proc sampler loses discovery latency and the final CPU delta at exit; CUBRID has no such exposure because its query workers are long-lived pooled threads inside one process, and its sampler U agrees with perf stat to +0.76%. R_wall, F_plan and F_work are unaffected and F_units x F_cpu telescopes to T_C/T_P regardless, so the correction moves only the SPLIT: F_units would be 0.519806 and F_cpu 3.482222. The card reports the SAMPLER values because Q01-Q21 did, keeping the factors comparable across the campaign, which makes the reported F_cpu an UPPER bound on CUBRID's CPU disadvantage and the reported F_units a LOWER bound on PostgreSQL's utilisation advantage.

POSTGRESQL LEAVES 3 OF ITS 5 CONTRACTED WORKERS UNUSED ON THE DOMINANT PIPELINE, reproducibly, and it is a PostgreSQL-side fact rather than a CUBRID improvement. The avg InitPlan's Gather launches 4 of 4 planned workers, then the main Gather Merge launches 1 of 4 planned -- 16 out of 16 observed executions across two probes (q22-pgworkers-probe.out, 12 runs in one connection; q22-pgworkers-control.out, 4 runs). The control isolates the cause: band probe B6, which has no InitPlan, launches 4 of 4 in 4 of 4 runs. Under the contracted max_parallel_workers=5 the InitPlan's four just-finished workers have not been reaped when the Gather Merge asks, so only one slot remains. PostgreSQL therefore wins Q22 by 1.810078x while running the expensive part at 2 units against CUBRID's 5 (U_P 2.02062 vs U_C 4.95333).

A DRIVER BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED MID-RUN, and the affected probe was re-measured. remeasure_all_guarded.sh declared its band-probe locals as 'local E=$1 B=$2 V=band${B} ...' on one line; bash expands ${B} there against the CALLER's B, not the one being declared. Inside the 'for B in B1..B7' loop the two were always equal so B1-B7 were measured and labelled correctly, but the single B8 call outside the loop inherited B7's label and re-ran B7 instead. B8 was then measured by remeasure_B8_guarded.sh, which declares each local on its own line; B7's retained artifacts are that second, equally valid B7 run.

Q22's traced statement costs 1.162 s against the 1.101 s headline (+5.5%): SET TRACE ON is instrumentation. No trace TIME is used anywhere in the report or the card; only readkeys / filteredkeys / rows / fetch / ioread / covered COUNTS are, and each is cross-checked against the independent ground-truth probe or against the PostgreSQL plan's own counters.
